relevance.rationale: Probes a 2d sinh dilaton gravity model whose asymptotic region geometrises the global symmetry of a q-deformed CFT, and finds q-deformed hyperbolic disk isometries emerging at the level of the two-point correlator. Two features make it more than topical for this folio. First, the deformation parameter is written q = e^{i pi b}, and the paper solves the SAME set of q-Ward identities in two separate ranges -- q on the unit circle and 0 < q < 1 -- obtaining different solutions in each. That two-regime structure is the corpus's own fibre-versus-observable split and its two-saddle reading of one object (rem:phi-b-bar-parity-interpretation: real-q Rogers saddle for mass, root-of-unity Faddeev saddle for decay), arrived at independently in a holographic setting. Second, the folio's gravity-spacetime chapter is explicitly a comparison chapter (rem:lqg-adm-ashtekar-comparison and its intro block compare against ADM, Ashtekar, LQG) and does not mention any q-deformed holography programme. Supporting: no result here is consumed by any derivation, and the two settings are only structurally analogous.

keyResults.locator: Sect. 2 (Correlation functions on the quantum disk)
keyResults.statement: The q-Ward identities for the two-point function admit distinct solutions depending on the range of q -- one for q = e^{i pi b} on the unit circle (analytic continuation to non-integer conformal weight), another for 0 < q < 1 -- with q-deformed hyperbolic disk isometries emerging in both.
keyResults.useForFolio: An independent instance of one q-object having two archimedean realisations selected by whether q sits on the unit circle or the real interval, which is the corpus's two-lens claim. What would need checking before any stronger statement: whether their b relates to the corpus's b = sqrt(t/2pi) e^{i pi/4} branch, and whether their two solutions are two faces of one function or two genuinely different objects.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; the gravity-spacetime comparison chapter is silent on q-deformed holography, which is the nearest live external programme to the folio's own q-deformed-geometry thesis.

A comparison remark in gravity-spacetime placing q-deformed holography alongside the existing ADM/Ashtekar/LQG entries. Kept as new-remark, not cite-in-block on rem:phi-b-bar-parity-interpretation, because the two-regime parallel is structural only and asserting more without checking the b conventions would be exactly the kind of resemblance-as-evidence the corpus rules against.
